top_choice_rationale: P001 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) rewards three separable, load-bearing contributions: the tractable pricing friction, staggered contracts with the policy rule, and the welfare-based synthesis. The work is 25 to 40 years old and has been extended rather than abandoned after 2008, the zero lower bound and the 2021-23 inflation. No earlier prize recognised the pricing-friction and policy-rule core, and its footprint on research and policy practice is the largest on the shortlist. My round-1 condition was a narrower citation that says which discovery each name is credited for, and the round-2 wording meets it. I weigh the count of supporters as no evidence of merit. The main cost is attribution: Galí, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans, Smets, Wouters and Gertler are excluded, and the citation cannot fully avoid implying a ranking against them. P002 (Kiyotaki, Moore) has the cleanest attribution and a mechanism distinct from the 2022 prize, but a narrower footprint and a mostly theoretical original contribution, so it ranks second. An award is preferable to no award because both proposals describe mature, original work.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile: no co-authorship or institutional link to Calvo, Taylor, Woodford, Kiyotaki or Moore. Disclosed only: thematic proximity to contracting-based mechanisms (Moore's incomplete-contracts lineage; staggered nominal contracts), long committee overlap with colleagues who support P001, and my role as KVA Vice President. Not adjudicated.
